brief: Goldman's industrials/materials morning note (Novak, 6 Oct) opens with market color (futures, FX, rates, commodities, overnight moves) then Privo's risk view: AI is called the cleanest part of the setup because inference demand looks more durable than appreciated and the desk is still short compute, offsetting investor worry over rates, oil, sovereign risk and midterms; net read is upside asymmetry into earnings, with a risk that a broadening rally follows if macro looks weak while micro (EPS) stays strong. On multi-industrials, Q1-Q2 saw accelerating year-over-year order growth, but Q3's macro backdrop (Middle East escalation, high oil, rising rates) should slow orders even as organic growth and topline beat consensus; rising input-cost inflation then pinches margins, netting in-line-ish earnings growth, with ETN the tactical pick on diversified end markets and light positioning. GIR's preview splits by subsector: Autos should post in-line-to-below-consensus results as soft China demand and Chinese OEM export gains hurt suppliers, prompting estimate/price-target cuts at APTV, VC, BWA, LEA and GNTX; Industrial Tech stays strong on datacenter capex and the industrial cycle but faces a high bar, with GIR raising estimates on APH, KEYS and TEL.
